subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or fail the tool call instead?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the report explicitly allows either warning or error behavior and that choice changes how a sandbox boundary is surfaced to users.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox routing disables explicit PTY while preserving the current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so users must choose gateway/elevated execution or remove the PTY request.

options.title: Adopt A Fork Fix After Decision
options.body: Review the open fork PR only after choosing the intended sandbox behavior and required proof.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox routing disables explicit PTY while preserving the current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest history signal for the original exec PTY behavior and adjacent fallback/runtime decisions.
